_note: Work queue for the remaining Food Detail profiles. status: queued -> drafted -> validated -> in-review -> approved (approval is an editorial decision made by the owner; nothing here is published). No profile is bundled until approved.

items.name: Mushrooms (button, shiitake)
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-3.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry covers button and shiitake; this is the white (button) mushroom record. Shiitake and others differ.

items.name: Kidney bean
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-5.json. Not published. REVIEW: Dried kidney beans must be boiled hard for 10 minutes (existing catalogue caution, carried over; not externally sourced).

items.name: Oyster
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-6.json. Not published. REVIEW: Six oysters provide about 33 mg of zinc, over four times the reference intake in one serving. NIH ODS lists a tolerable upper intake for zinc, but that value has not been read this session: check it before publishing and consider a caution or a smaller serving.

items.name: Sardine
items.preparationState: canned in oil, drained, with bones

items.name: Miso
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: Miso is very high in sodium (existing catalogue caution: high in salt). Sodium is not in the key list and no sourced salt caution has been added.

items.name: Grapefruit
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-4.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry "grapefruit" is not specific; this is the pink and red record. White grapefruit has less vitamin A.

items.name: Beef
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry "beef" is generic. The record is 90% lean ground beef, cooked; steaks, roasts and fattier mince differ.

items.name: Anchovies
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-6.json. Not published. REVIEW: Canned anchovies are very salty; sodium is not shown and no salt caution has a source yet.

items.name: Tempeh
items.preparationState: as sold (fermented soybean cake), not cooked

items.name: White beans
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-5.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry "white beans" covers cannellini, navy and great northern; this is the USDA "white" record.

items.name: White potato
items.preparationState: baked, flesh and skin, no salt

items.name: Lettuce (Bibb, Boston, romaine)
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-3.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry covers Bibb, Boston and romaine; this is the romaine record. Other lettuces differ.

items.name: Brazil nut
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-5.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue limit is 1–2 nuts a day, so the serving is 2 kernels. Brazil nuts are extremely high in selenium; selenium is not in the key list (no selenium reference was read this session) and the limit comes from the existing catalogue caution, not re-sourced here.

items.name: Chicken
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry "chicken" is generic; the record is skinless breast. Thighs and skin-on cuts have more fat and more iron and zinc.

items.name: Sauerkraut
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: Canned sauerkraut is pasteurised; raw, refrigerated sauerkraut keeps live cultures, which a nutrient record does not capture. It is high in sodium (existing caution).

items.name: Canned salmon
items.preparationState: canned pink salmon, drained solids (with skin and bones)

items.name: Canned tuna
items.preparationState: canned light tuna in water, drained
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-6.json. Not published. REVIEW: Light (skipjack) tuna, a "Best Choice" in FDA/EPA advice. Albacore (white) tuna is a different record and a "Good Choice".

items.name: Farro
items.preparationState: dry, uncooked, pearled (no cooked farro record in USDA)
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-5.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA has only a DRY pearled farro record (Foundation); amounts are before cooking. Whole (unpearled) farro has more fibre.

items.name: Hummus
items.preparationState: prepared, commercial (contains tahini, oil and salt)
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-5.json. Not published. REVIEW: A prepared food that varies by brand (salt, oil, tahini); the record is the USDA commercial average.

items.name: Plain yogurt
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: Whole-milk plain yogurt; low-fat and fat-free versions have similar protein and calcium with less fat. Vitamin D is only present if the milk is fortified.

items.name: Crab
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-6.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry "crab" is generic; the record is Alaska king crab.

items.name: Pickles
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: Vinegar pickles are not live-fermented; fermented pickles differ. Very high in sodium (existing caution), not shown.

items.name: Asparagus
items.preparationState: cooked, boiled, drained (USDA record is without added salt where stated; this record has none listed)

items.name: Bean sprouts
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-3.json. Not published. REVIEW: Catalogue "bean sprouts" is read as mung bean sprouts, the common kind. Raw sprouts carry a food-safety caution (FDA/USDA) that has not been added; see the editorial list.

items.name: Kefir
items.preparationState: low-fat plain kefir (a branded USDA record)
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: The only USDA kefir records are branded (Lifeway); values for other kefirs differ, and live-culture content is not in a nutrient record.

items.name: Sea bass
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-6.json. Not published. REVIEW: "Sea bass" is ambiguous. FDA/EPA lists black sea bass as a Best Choice and Chilean sea bass as a Good Choice (more mercury). The USDA record is "sea bass, mixed species". Decide which fish the catalogue means before publishing.

items.name: Tofu
items.preparationState: raw (as sold), firm, set with calcium sulfate
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: Calcium depends on the coagulant: tofu set with calcium sulfate is high in calcium, tofu set with nigari (magnesium chloride) is not. The record is the calcium-sulfate type.

items.name: Pork
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry "pork" is generic; the record is roasted lean loin. Other cuts, and processed pork, differ.

items.name: Barley
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-5.json. Not published. REVIEW: Pearled barley has had part of its bran removed; hulled barley has more fibre.

items.name: Nut butter
items.preparationState: smooth peanut butter, no added salt
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-5.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry "nut butter" is generic (the existing caution says tree-nut or peanut allergen, depending on type). The record is peanut butter; almond butter and others differ.

items.name: Red lentil
items.preparationState: dry, uncooked (no cooked red-lentil record in USDA)
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-5.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA has no cooked red-lentil record, so amounts are for the DRY lentils; red lentils roughly triple in weight when cooked. The profile says so.

items.name: Lamb
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry "lamb" is generic; the record is roasted lean leg (shank half). Other cuts differ.

items.name: Salmon
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-6.json. Not published. REVIEW: Farmed Atlantic salmon; wild salmon differs (less fat, less omega-3).

items.name: Squash
items.preparationState: baked, no salt, all winter varieties
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-3.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry "squash" is not specific. This is the USDA record for winter squash, all varieties, baked; butternut, acorn and others vary.

items.name: Sweet potato
items.preparationState: baked in skin, flesh only, no salt

items.name: Turkey
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: Roasted breast, meat only; dark meat and deli turkey differ.

items.name: Greek yogurt
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA lists no household measure for this record; 170 g (a 6-ounce container) is my choice, not USDA's. The catalogue entry is generic: fat-free Greek yogurt has less fat and similar protein.

items.name: Kimchi
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-7.json. Not published. REVIEW: Kimchi recipes vary (fish sauce, salt, chilli); the record is a USDA average. It is high in sodium; no caution is recorded in the catalogue.

items.name: Mackerel
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-6.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry "mackerel" is generic; the record is Atlantic mackerel. A caution about king mackerel (a different, high-mercury fish) is added.

items.name: Mixed nuts
items.preparationState: dry roasted, with peanuts, no salt added
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-5.json. Not published. REVIEW: A blend that varies by product; the record is a USDA dry-roasted mix with peanuts and no added salt.

items.name: Snapper
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-6.json. Not published. REVIEW: The record is snapper, mixed species, not specifically red snapper.

items.name: Whole-grain bread
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-5.json. Not published. REVIEW: Commercial breads vary a lot (fibre, salt, added calcium). The record is a USDA average of whole-wheat bread, which is not necessarily whole GRAIN bread.

items.name: Dulse
items.notes: BLOCKED: No USDA FoodData Central record for dulse (searched SR Legacy and Foundation). Needs a verified composition source before a profile.

items.name: Hijiki
items.notes: BLOCKED: No USDA record for hijiki. Hijiki also has a known inorganic-arsenic concern raised by food-safety agencies; a sourced caution (not read for this project) would be needed before any profile.

items.name: Kelp
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: Raw kelp. Iodine can exceed the safe limit (existing catalogue cautions: carried over, not externally sourced here; NIH ODS has an iodine fact sheet that has not been read this session).

items.name: Kombu
items.notes: BLOCKED: No USDA record for kombu (dried kelp). Raw kelp (168457) exists and is drafted as 'kelp', but it is a different preparation (raw vs dried) and was not used as a stand-in. Iodine content is very high and needs a sourced caution.

items.name: Wakame
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: Raw (as USDA lists it); dried wakame is far more concentrated by weight. Seaweed iodine content is not in a nutrient record here; the existing catalogue caution ("Iodine: normal portions") is carried over without an external source.

items.name: Concord grape
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-9.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA's American-type slip-skin grape is the Concord type. Grape juice is a different food.

items.name: Adzuki bean
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA lists no vitamin E or K values for this record.

items.name: Black soybean
items.notes: BLOCKED: No USDA record for black soybeans. The yellow soybean record (174271) is a different variety and was not substituted without owner approval.

items.name: Chestnut
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: Unlike most nuts, chestnuts are low in fat and high in starch. Raw, boiled and dried chestnuts differ; the record is roasted.

items.name: Duck
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: Meat only without skin. Duck with skin has far more fat.

items.name: Catfish
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-11.json. Not published. REVIEW: Farmed channel catfish, the type sold in the US. Wild and imported catfish differ.

items.name: Octopus
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-11.json. Not published. REVIEW: The USDA record shows 36 µg of vitamin B12 per 100 g, about fifteen times the adult reference intake in one serving. It is the figure USDA publishes, but it is unusually high and was flagged for a second look rather than rounded or adjusted.

items.name: Squid
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-11.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA also has a fried (battered) squid record with more fat and carbohydrate (175 kcal per 85 g); the raw record is used here because the catalogue does not say it is fried.

items.name: Bancha tea
items.notes: BLOCKED: Brewed tea has almost no nutrients in USDA records and any caffeine/fluoride/tannin message needs a sourced caution. Needs an editorial decision on format.

items.name: Decaf coffee
items.notes: BLOCKED: As coffee: almost no nutrients; residual caffeine and sourcing need an editorial decision.

items.name: Salt
items.notes: BLOCKED: Not a nutrient-offering food: salt supplies sodium (and iodine only if iodised), and sodium guidance (e.g. the Dietary Guidelines limit) is a safety/limit message, not a 'what this food offers' profile. Needs an editorial decision on format before any draft.

items.name: Tamari
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-12.json. Not published. REVIEW: Tamari is very high in sodium (not shown in this nutrient set); the USDA record is a generic tamari. Tamari is often sold as wheat-free but labels vary, so people avoiding gluten should check the label.

items.name: Rye
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: The USDA record is dry rye grain. Cooked rye berries absorb water, so a cup of cooked grain has much less per cup. Rye bread, rye flour and rye crackers are separate foods. Contains gluten.

items.name: Wheat
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry "Wheat" does not say which wheat; USDA's durum wheat grain was used, and hard red or soft wheat berries differ somewhat. Dry, uncooked grain. USDA lists no fibre value for this record, so fibre is not shown. Contains gluten.

items.name: Lemon
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-9.json. Not published. REVIEW: Whole lemon without peel; most people use juice or a wedge, so the serving here is much larger than a squeeze.

items.name: Lime
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-9.json. Not published. REVIEW: A whole lime is a larger serving than the juice or wedge people usually use.

items.name: Sour cherry
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-9.json. Not published. REVIEW: Raw sour cherries; tart cherry juice and dried cherries are separate foods.

items.name: Mung bean
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: Whole mung beans; sprouted mung beans have their own record.

items.name: Fresh-water clam
items.notes: BLOCKED: USDA has only marine/mixed clam records; freshwater clam composition differs. The catalogue marks it not ship-ready.

items.name: Soft-shell crab
items.notes: BLOCKED: Soft-shell crab is blue crab caught after moulting and eaten whole, usually fried. USDA has cooked blue crab (174205) but not soft-shell crab, so the preparation and whole-animal composition differ. Needs a decision on whether blue crab may stand in.

items.name: Olives
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: Canned ripe olives show a lot of iron in the USDA record (6.3 mg per 100 g); that is partly iron added in processing, so the iron may not be representative of other olives. Very high in sodium (existing caution); sodium not shown.

items.name: Vinegar
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-12.json. Not published. REVIEW: The record is cider vinegar; other vinegars (balsamic, rice, wine) differ. A tablespoon supplies almost no nutrients. This profile makes no claim about blood sugar, weight or digestion.

items.name: Amaranth
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Cooked amaranth grain; amaranth leaves are a different food. USDA lists no folate, vitamin A, C or K values for this record.

items.name: Corn
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: Sweet corn eaten as a vegetable; popcorn and cornmeal are separate foods.

items.name: Chicory
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: The record is chicory greens; chicory root (as in coffee substitutes) is different.

items.name: Endive
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA "endive" is curly endive; Belgian endive (witloof, a chicory) is a different vegetable.

items.name: Escarole
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA has only a cooked escarole record (escarole is commonly eaten raw too; raw would have more vitamin C).

items.name: Coconut
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-9.json. Not published. REVIEW: Raw coconut meat. Coconut milk, coconut water and coconut oil are separate foods with different composition. This is a high-fat food (about 34 g per 100 g, mostly saturated); no amount is recommended here.

items.name: Persimmon
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-9.json. Not published. REVIEW: Japanese persimmon, the common supermarket type. USDA's "native" (American) persimmon record is a different fruit with sparse data and was not used. Dried persimmon is far more concentrated.

items.name: Tuna
items.preparationState: light tuna, canned in water, no salt, drained
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-11.json. Not published. REVIEW: Canned light tuna, matching the catalogue caution "prefer light/skipjack". Fresh tuna, albacore and bigeye are different records with different mercury levels; this profile does not cover them. Mercury advice for tuna was not looked up for this draft beyond the catalogue caution.

items.name: Alcohol (moderate)
items.notes: BLOCKED: 'Alcohol (moderate)' is not a nutrient-offering food, and any profile would be a health-risk message that needs expert/editorial wording (Dietary Guidelines, NIAAA). Needs an owner decision on whether to profile it at all.

items.name: Chocolate
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-12.json. Not published. REVIEW: Dark chocolate 70–85% cacao; milk and white chocolate are different foods. Caffeine and theobromine are not in this nutrient set. Mineral content (iron, magnesium) comes with about 170 kcal and 12 g of fat per ounce.

items.name: Coffee
items.notes: BLOCKED: Brewed coffee has almost no nutrients in USDA records; caffeine guidance (FDA, pregnancy) needs sourced wording that was not read for this project. Needs an editorial decision.

items.name: Ketchup
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-12.json. Not published. REVIEW: A condiment with added sugar and salt; a tablespoon supplies little of any nutrient. Sodium and added sugar are not shown in this nutrient set.

items.name: Turmeric
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-12.json. Not published. REVIEW: Ground turmeric as a spice. Per 100 g it has very high iron (55 mg), but a teaspoon is 3 g, so it adds about 1.7 mg at most. Curcumin content is not in this record, and this profile makes no claim about turmeric supplements or inflammation.

items.name: Date
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-9.json. Not published. REVIEW: Medjool dates; the existing catalogue entry does not say which variety, and deglet noor dates differ somewhat. Dates are concentrated in sugar (about 66 g per 100 g by the record's carbohydrate).

items.name: Raisin
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-9.json. Not published. REVIEW: Dark seedless raisins; golden raisins (often treated with sulphites) are a separate USDA record.

items.name: Hickory
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA lists no vitamin E or K values for this record.

items.name: Pine nut
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: Pine nuts as sold in shops. USDA's pinyon pine nut is a separate record.

items.name: Mint
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue has mint and peppermint separately; this is spearmint. The USDA record shows very high iron per 100 g (11.9 mg), but a normal use of mint is a few leaves, so the serving figures are small.

items.name: Peppermint
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: Peppermint tea or peppermint oil are different from the fresh leaf; a nutrient record does not cover any effect of them.

items.name: Spirulina
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-12.json. Not published. REVIEW: Dried spirulina. Quality, contamination and vitamin B12 forms differ between products and are not covered by this record (USDA lists B12 as 0).

items.name: Almond milk
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-13.json. Not published. REVIEW: The calcium, vitamin D and vitamin E in this record come from fortification, and brands differ; an unfortified almond drink has far less calcium. Almond drinks contain little almond and little protein (0.4 g per 100 g).

items.name: Avocado oil
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-12.json. Not published. REVIEW: A pure oil: about 14 g of fat and 124 kcal per tablespoon with no meaningful vitamins or minerals in the USDA record.

items.name: Bacon
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: A cured, processed meat that is high in salt and fat (sodium is not shown here). No sourced caution was added beyond the catalogue's own.

items.name: Bagel
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Plain enriched bagel; whole-grain and flavoured bagels differ. Iron and folate come largely from enrichment. A medium bagel is about 275 kcal and is a large serving of refined grain.

items.name: Baked beans
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: Canned baked beans in sauce, which usually contains added sugar and salt (not shown in this nutrient set); varies by brand.

items.name: Butter
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-13.json. Not published. REVIEW: Mostly fat (about 11.5 g and 102 kcal per tablespoon), mostly saturated. Salted butter; unsalted differs in sodium (not shown).

items.name: Canned tomatoes
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: This record is canned in juice with salt; a no-salt-added record also exists (170138).

items.name: Cheddar cheese
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-13.json. Not published. REVIEW: Sharp cheddar; mild and aged cheddars differ a little. Cheese is also high in sodium and saturated fat (not shown here).

items.name: Coconut oil
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-12.json. Not published. REVIEW: A pure oil, mostly saturated fat; no meaningful vitamins or minerals. The record is coconut oil (not hydrogenated). This profile makes no health claim about coconut oil.

items.name: Couscous
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Standard (semolina) couscous, which is a wheat pasta and contains gluten; whole-wheat and pearl (Israeli) couscous differ.

items.name: Cranberry
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-9.json. Not published. REVIEW: Raw cranberries (tart). Dried sweetened cranberries and cranberry juice are different foods.

items.name: Cream cheese
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-13.json. Not published. REVIEW: Regular full-fat cream cheese; reduced-fat and whipped versions differ. Soft cheeses have their own safety questions in pregnancy that were not researched for this draft.

items.name: Dried apricots
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-9.json. Not published. REVIEW: Sulfured dried apricots (the orange kind); unsulfured ones are brown and the record differs. Sulphite sensitivity is a real caution for sulphited dried fruit; the catalogue caution is carried over without an external source here.

items.name: Egg noodles
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Enriched egg noodles, cooked; folate and iron come mainly from enrichment. Contain egg and wheat.

items.name: Fava (broad) beans
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: Dried fava beans, cooked. Fresh young fava pods are a different food.

items.name: Fennel
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: The bulb. Fennel seeds are a spice with different amounts.

items.name: Granola
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA's homemade granola. Shop-bought granola varies a lot (many contain much more sugar), so the numbers are a rough guide only. A typical bowlful is much more than 1 oz.

items.name: Guacamole
items.notes: BLOCKED: No USDA SR Legacy record for guacamole; composition varies by recipe (avocado, onion, lime, salt). Needs a defined recipe or a branded product.

items.name: Ham
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: A cured, processed meat that is high in salt (sodium not shown here). Deli ham varies by brand.

items.name: Hemp seeds
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: Hulled hemp seed. Omega-3 and vitamin K are not given in this USDA record, so they are not shown.

items.name: Herring
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-11.json. Not published. REVIEW: Cooked fresh herring; pickled and smoked herring (common in shops) are different and much saltier.

items.name: Honey
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-12.json. Not published. REVIEW: Honey is mostly sugar: about 17 g of carbohydrate and 64 kcal per tablespoon with trace minerals.

items.name: Maple syrup
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-12.json. Not published. REVIEW: Pure maple syrup, not pancake-syrup blends. Mostly sugar: about 13 g of carbohydrate and 52 kcal per tablespoon.

items.name: Milk
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-13.json. Not published. REVIEW: The catalogue entry does not say whole milk or skim; whole milk (3.25% fat) was used, and reduced-fat milks have less fat and energy but similar calcium. Raw (unpasteurised) milk is a different matter and is not covered.

items.name: Muesli
items.notes: BLOCKED: No generic USDA record for muesli (only brand cereals such as Alpen and Familia). Needs a defined product.

items.name: Naan
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Commercial plain naan; restaurant naan often contains butter or ghee and differs. USDA lists no folate, vitamin A, C or K values for this record.

items.name: Oat milk
items.notes: BLOCKED: No USDA SR Legacy record for oat milk; composition is brand-specific (fortification, added oil, sugar). Needs a defined product or label data.

items.name: Olive oil
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-12.json. Not published. REVIEW: The USDA record is olive oil for salad or cooking; extra-virgin oil may have other compounds that are not in this nutrient set.

items.name: Parmesan
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-13.json. Not published. REVIEW: Grated parmesan as sold in shakers or tubs, which can include added ingredients and is lower in water than a wedge; a hard wedge has a slightly different composition. Very salty (sodium not shown).

items.name: Pasta
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Regular enriched wheat pasta, cooked. Folate and iron come largely from enrichment. Whole-wheat pasta is a separate profile.

items.name: Plantain
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: Plantain is normally cooked (fried, boiled, baked); frying adds fat. The record is raw yellow plantain; no cooked record was chosen.

items.name: Polenta / cornmeal
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Dry whole-grain cornmeal. Polenta is cooked with several times its weight in water, so one cooked cup has far less per cup. Degermed (more common) cornmeal has less fibre and minerals.

items.name: Popcorn (plain)
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Plain air-popped popcorn. Microwave and cinema popcorn have butter, oil and salt added, which this record does not show.

items.name: Rice cakes
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Plain brown-rice cakes; flavoured and white-rice versions differ.

items.name: Rice noodles
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Plain cooked rice noodles; they are naturally wheat-free but labels vary.

items.name: Rye bread
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Commercial US rye bread, which is often part wheat; a dense 100% rye loaf differs. Contains gluten.

items.name: Salsa
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-8.json. Not published. REVIEW: A prepared food that varies by brand; high in sodium (no sourced caution added).

items.name: Seitan
items.notes: BLOCKED: No USDA record for seitan. Values depend on the product (vital wheat gluten content, added soy sauce, salt). Needs a defined product.

items.name: Smoked salmon
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-11.json. Not published. REVIEW: Cold-smoked chinook (lox). Vitamin D, E and K are not given in the lox record (the other smoked chinook record, 173687, gives vitamin D 17.1 µg per 100 g). It is a salty, cured food (sodium not shown), and the catalogue lists no caution; preparation and pregnancy cautions for smoked fish were not looked up for this draft.

items.name: Soba noodles
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA lists no fibre value. Many soba noodles are part wheat; 100% buckwheat soba is different, and wheat content matters for gluten.

items.name: Sour cream
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-13.json. Not published. REVIEW: Regular full-fat sour cream; reduced-fat versions differ.

items.name: Sourdough bread
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA groups sourdough with French and Vienna bread in one record; an artisan sourdough loaf may differ. Contains gluten; no claim is made about fermentation, digestion or blood sugar.

items.name: Soy milk
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-13.json. Not published. REVIEW: The USDA record is UNFORTIFIED soy milk; most shop-bought soy milk is fortified with calcium (and often vitamin D and B12), so its calcium is much higher than shown. Sweetened versions have more sugar.

items.name: Tahini
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-10.json. Not published. REVIEW: USDA has several tahini records (roasted, raw, unroasted); the "kernels unspecified" one was chosen because the catalogue does not specify. Values differ between them, notably calcium.

items.name: Tortillas (wheat)
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Flour (wheat) tortilla; corn tortillas are a different food. Sizes vary a lot.

items.name: Wheat flour (whole-grain)
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Dry flour, as an ingredient; values apply to the flour, not to the finished baked goods.

items.name: White rice
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-14.json. Not published. REVIEW: Enriched white rice; folate and iron come largely from enrichment. Brown, basmati and sushi rice are separate foods.

items.name: Heavy cream
items.notes: Draft in draft-batch-13.json. Not published. REVIEW: High in fat (about 5.4 g and 51 kcal per tablespoon).
